_note:
THE SHEER FIXTURE. A hull and one swept bulwark. Nothing else: no mast, no deckhouse, no rig, no fittings — because the claim under test is about the SILHOUETTE, and a fixture with a mast in it lets a bad silhouette hide behind a good mast. Squint at the capture: what should read is a working boat's deck edge sweeping up toward the stem, and that curve is the only thing this fixture draws. Its control is probe_sheer_bulwark_flat.json, which is this file with follow_sheer false and is the two-parallel-bars shape the trawler fixtures read as today. The two are meant to be looked at side by side.

The bulwark is ONE edges[] entry. Its cap is not a number in this file and must never become one: `from_hull` means the run is resolved through StructureEdge.sheer_bulwark_spec against HullStations, so the cap Y at every station is deck_y + sheer_rise_at(z) + height, and sheer_rise_at is freeboard x the hull form's own bow/stern keel rise. Six hulls in the catalog, one rule, no per-hull tuning: retune fine_entry's bow_keel_rise and every fine-entry hull's sheer moves with it. The only authored length here is `height` — the cap AMIDSHIPS, 1.1 m, which is a fall-barrier dimension set by the 1.8 m figure and is the same on a trawler and on a freighter.

The `hull` block below restates hull_28x10's catalog numbers so the gate test can build HullStations without naming a vessel script (the --script lane cannot name autoload identifiers, and BoatBody's dependency chain reaches them). tests/vessel_render_capture.gd asserts these numbers — loa, beam, deck_y and both ends of the sheer — against the hull it actually spawns, so the restatement cannot drift.

COLOUR IS DOING SILHOUETTE WORK, on purpose and for free. The plating is the topsides colour and the cap is pale, so hull and bulwark read as ONE body whose top edge is the sheer — rather than as a hull with a pale bar sitting on it, which is exactly what the current fixtures read as. Both rides in the vertex stream on one material, so the whole bulwark is one surface and costs no draw call.

hull._note: hull_28x10, as FishingTrawlerSmall.make_physics_profile() builds it: 14 x 5 x 2.8 m at WORLD_FEEL_SCALE 2, i.e. a 28 x 10 m vessel with 5.6 m depth and 2.8 m draft. Freeboard 2.8 m x fine_entry bow_keel_rise 0.32 = 0.896 m of sheer forward, 2.8 x 0.10 = 0.28 m aft. Derived, not written down.

edges._is: bulwark, both sides and the transom, capped — the deck edge of the vessel
